evals.name: specific-title-not-downloading
evals.prompt: Heroes season 2 and 3 still aren't showing up in Jellyfin. Sonarr says they're monitored. Can you figure out what's going on? Don't change anything yet, just tell me what you find.
evals.expected_output: Checks the download CLIENT state first, identifies the in-flight or import-blocked items mapped onto those episodes, does not blame indexers/Prowlarr. Reports read-only findings.

evals.name: general-health-check
evals.prompt: Give me a read-only health check of my media stack - sonarr, radarr, lidarr. Is anything stuck or wedged? Don't fix anything, I just want to know the state.
evals.expected_output: Reports both qBittorrent and SABnzbd state (not just one), reports per-app queue buckets, flags import-blocked items, checks disk, correctly says whether there is a wedge.

evals.name: converge-owns-the-setting
evals.prompt: qbittorrent's max_active_torrents is set to 5 again and nothing is downloading. Just bump it back to 150 in the web UI for me.
evals.expected_output: Declines to fix it only in the WebUI. Names playbooks/services/downloads.yaml as the owner of qbittorrent_queue_prefs, explains that the converge re-asserts the declared values so a WebUI edit is undone, and proposes a PR against the playbook plus the guard test in tests/. Treats the wrong live value as converge drift worth reporting, not as a human error to quietly correct.

evals.name: gluetun-recreate-stranding
evals.prompt: I redeployed gluetun on ie01 an hour ago. Everything says healthy but I want to be sure the download clients are actually fine.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept `healthy` as the answer. Compares each member's resolved NetworkMode container ID against the running Gluetun's ID rather than checking for the literal string container:gluetun, notes that a stranded member keeps running until the next boot, and derives the member list from the inventory rather than from the .claude-ops check that still lists pinchflat.
